title: Deeds as soil, the Word as seed
hookLine: make good deeds the soil and the Word the seed, and water it with truth (Sri Rag, ang 24)

lines: THE SEED IS THE EASY PART.
cards: Ask any farmer in the Punjab, or anyone who's kept a tomato plant alive on a balcony: the seed is the easy part. A packet costs almost nothing.
What decides the harvest is the ground you put it in, and whether you water it, day after day, when nothing seems to be happening.
Tradition remembers Guru Nanak as a farmer in his last years, and his hymns are full of fields, plows and rain. On day 145 we heard one of them, the mind as plowman.
Today, a different one: a whole spiritual life in a single line.

teach.b: On Ang 24, in Sri Rag, Guru Nanak sings: amal kar dhartee beej sabdo kar sach kee aab nit dehi paanee. Make your deeds the earth, make the Word the seed, and water it every day with the water of truth.
Then, in paraphrase: become that kind of farmer, and faith will sprout. Three parts. Amal, deeds, is the soil.

teach.h: SABAD — THE WORD IS THE SEED.
teach.b: Sabad, the Guru's Word, is the seed.

Sach, yesterday's word, is the water, and nit means every day. Each needs the others. A beautiful seed in hard, stony ground won't grow: that's someone who hears wonderful hymns and changes nothing in how they act.
Good soil with no seed is honest work with no remembering. And soil and seed with no water is a promising start that dries out by Thursday. The picture says something quiet about time, too.
Farmers don't dig up a seed every morning to see if it's working.
The next line says whoever farms this way comes to understand heaven and hell, and many readers hear in it that both grow from how you live. It fits the man who sang it.
Tradition tells that after decades of travel, Guru Nanak settled at Kartarpur on the Ravi River and worked the land himself, with a community that farmed, sang and ate together.
The teacher of the Word was also a man with dirt under his nails.

how: Sikhs often cite Guru Nanak's years farming at Kartarpur as the model of a householder's life, joining honest work, remembering the Name and sharing, and his farming images are sung in kirtan.

o: deeds, the soil a spiritual life grows in
rain that falls on a farmer's fields
the seed of the Guru's Word in the heart

games.q: Guru Nanak's farm — tap the pairs.

s: in this hymn, the Word is the soil and deeds are the seed
deeds are the soil, the Word is the seed, and truth is the water.
tradition says Guru Nanak farmed at Kartarpur in his later years
after long travels he settled on the Ravi and worked the land.
the hymn says the water should be given every day
nit dehi paanee: water it daily with truth.

games.q: you've heard beautiful hymns for years, but nothing in how you act has changed. in Guru Nanak's picture, what's missing?
o: the soil: good deeds for the Word to grow in.
games.why: a fine seed in stony ground won't grow. amal kar dhartee: make your deeds the earth.

practice: Imagine a small patch of ground: that's today.
Choose one good deed to plant in it, a meal cooked for someone, a bill paid on time, an hour of help, a kind word to someone who won't expect it, and see yourself putting it in the ground.
You don't need to watch it grow, only to water it; rest with the breath, patient as a farmer.

wordCard.voice: Amal, deeds, the soil of the spiritual life. Guru Nanak's farming picture in Sri Rag: good deeds are the ground, the Word is the seed, and truth, given every day, is the water.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: amal, deeds; a word from Persian and Arabic that Guru Nanak uses for the soil of the spiritual life.

carryVoice: Your line: deeds are the soil. No digging it up to check. Two hundred fifty days, and counting.
